case_title: C. Muniappan & Ors. v. State of Tamil Nadu
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.307; TN (POL) Act s.3, 4
aggravating_circumstances: Extreme brutality, previous planning, exceptional depravity, unprovoked attack on helpless, innocent, unarmed young girl students
high_court_outcome: Confirmed death sentences for A-2 to A-4, modified sentences for others to run concurrently
neutral_facts: During a political agitation, a group of agitators set fire to a university bus carrying female students, resulting in the deaths of three girls and burn injuries to several others. The accused were involved in the act of setting the bus ablaze, with some of them sprinkling petrol inside the bus before igniting it. The incident occurred during a peaceful demonstration that turned violent when the agitators targeted public transport vehicles. The accused were identified through witness accounts and evidence, including statements from witnesses and photographic evidence of the scene. The trial court convicted the accused under various sections of the Indian Penal Code and the Tamil Nadu Police Act, with the High Court confirming the death sentences for the main perpetrators and modifying the sentences for others to run concurrently.
